comments.@0413n0vdeasm4n7clkjvu6t2km: Where the top of the parabola through three evenly spaced values is, from the middle one: 0 when the middle is the top, between −½ and ½ when it is the highest of the three.
comments.@3t9kuhfn8j29de2lsfaj7qgqg9: The cross correlation of the samples with themselves: high at a lag the signal repeats after, so a note's period is its first high lag past 0.
comments.@71fh1hu6umbnujgl8nvilssuv5: n weights rising from 0 to 1 and back, ½ − ½cos(2πi/(n − 1)): a block multiplied by them has no edges, so its spectrum doesn't smear. Hann's window (Blackman and Tukey, 1958).
comments.@9mk4jepkbthrmg0n5nar2bichl: The discrete Fourier transform of a list of complex numbers: item k is Σ x_j·e^(−2πi·jk/n). Any length; a power of two takes n log n steps. Cooley and Tukey's radix-2 split (1965).
comments.@9q6crvcenooqe3viu9nkauisur: A helper of peaks. Not offered.
comments.@acv9rqun5h0qm6m0fmfc9uiv5e: The smallest power of two that is at least n: the length an FFT is quickest at.
comments.@d0g10ri987854pk815mjrc4vba: The transform as written, n² steps. A helper of fft for lengths with no 2 in them. Not offered.
comments.@haobtdi6pdmblq6j31qe3sues1: The fft of real samples: item k is how much of k cycles per length there is, as a complex number (its modulus the amount, its angle the phase).
comments.@hl09u7mo6f69fk4t9hj6a20o8q: The samples with zeros after them, to size items in all.
comments.@i3j8cm5g55r0vcp1pvc9a0b75a: The inverse of fft: inverse fft(fft(xs)) is xs again.
comments.@lhu571jdbqghl89h30thk573au: Every place a value is higher than both its neighbours, as (place, height), each read between samples off the parabola through the three (quadratic interpolation).
comments.@mughnivmrc93kcno0i5k7jtuaq: The fft of n items of an array, from start, step apart, as an array, by the whole length's roots of unity. A helper of fft. Not offered.
comments.@os8kak0cb1svkgpagfvl4shquv: The samples multiplied by a Hann window as long as they are.
comments.@q4e9fi14opg6damuelud2tbv57: A helper of power of two at least. Not offered.
comments.@u3g1bo95l94sm374b0k1ub85ad: For each lag from 0 to length(a) − 1, Σ a[i + lag]·b[i]: how strongly b turns up in a that many samples late. By FFT (Wiener–Khinchin), so n log n.
